name: Baked Ham & Cheese Party Sandwiches
headnote: LisaT's own note runs to one sentence, saying these baked sliders suit any party and that even fussy eaters will eat them. The editorial text (contributions by Rai Mincey) fills in the rest, describing buttery rolls filled with deli ham, Swiss and sharp Dijon and noting they work as either an appetiser or a main. It also covers storage: about two days refrigerated, reheated covered at 350F, or frozen up to six months and thawed overnight before baking. There is no explanation of the technique beyond pouring the butter-mustard mixture over the assembled rolls.
comment_digest: The top review (440 helpful, Karengtyler) says to pour the entire butter mixture over the rolls rather than holding any back, because it soaks in as they bake; she doubled the Dijon and swapped poppy seeds for minced garlic and onion powder. A later reviewer (26 helpful) disagrees, arguing the original King's Hawaiian version reserves some to brush the tops and pours the rest before the roll tops go on, since pouring it all over leaves soggy bottoms and hard tops. The most repeated correction is the bake: cover with foil for the first 10 minutes or most of the time and finish uncovered, or the tops dry out and burn; parchment underneath prevents scorched bottoms. Everything bagel seasoning is the standard poppy seed substitute, and cheddar, muenster, provolone or havarti all get good reports. Hawaiian rolls are near-universal; slicing before baking makes serving easier.
